description: Heinz Wilhelm Guderian (German: [haɪnts ˈvɪlhɛlm ɡuˈdeːʁi.an]; 17 June 1888 – 14 May 1954) was a German army general and military theorist. A pioneer and advocate of the "blitzkrieg" approach, he played a central role in the development of the panzer division concept and tank warfare more broadly. After serving in the military since leaving school, including in World War I, in 1936, he was promoted to Heer Generalmajor (Major General) and became the Inspector of Motorized Troops.
